target: Designers, software developers, marketers, and professionals handling media files on macOS and Windows
where: Global (US, Europe, India, Remote Tech Hubs)

behaviours.name: Daily media converter
behaviours.how: Converts screenshots, webp images, and mp4 clips multiple times a day for Slack, GitHub, or social media.

behaviours.name: Privacy-conscious professional
behaviours.how: Handles sensitive client files, designs, or contracts and cannot upload to third-party web converters.

behaviours.name: Anti-subscription pragmatist
behaviours.how: Refuses monthly SaaS subscriptions for basic utility tools; happily pays once for solid lifetime software.

behaviours.name: CLI & power user
behaviours.how: Knows FFmpeg and ImageMagick, but finds terminal syntax tedious for quick 5-second file adjustments.

behaviours.name: Occasional converter
behaviours.how: Only converts or merges PDFs and videos once or twice a month and looks for simplicity.

behaviours.name: Tool collector & Mac/PC enthusiast
behaviours.how: Loves polished productivity tools (CleanShot, Raycast) that make their desktop workflow feel premium.

objections: I can just use free websites like CloudConvert or TinyPNG
$19 is steep for a file converter when free alternatives exist
I already know how to use FFmpeg or ImageOptim in terminal
Will this hog memory or drain my battery running in the menu bar?
Do I really need another background resident app?
Can I trust an indie app with system accessibility permissions?
habits: you frequently share screen recordings and GIFs with your remote team
you get annoyed when websites save images as .webp instead of .png
you redact and merge PDF contracts or client invoices every week
you work across both a Mac laptop and a Windows desktop
